transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy new year, we'll run through how teams are using Redwood for embeddings and reranking, quick intros?
[00:12] Priya (Celestia): Hi, Priya here, CTO, Alex and Nina are with me. We're evaluating infra for semantic search and a rerank layer for our clinical search product.
[00:24] Alex (Celestia): Yep, our main questions are: can you hook into our vector DB, what's the latency at 100 QPS, and whether we should use Redwood Hosted or Dedicated.
[00:35] Jordan (Redwood, SE): Great, thanks. Quick question on current stack — what are you using for vectordb indexing today?
[00:42] Nina (Celestia): We're prototyping with Milvus and a Postgres + FAISS pipeline. Also spinning up a small Pinecone trial, but ops wants more control.
[00:52] Maya: Nice, that's common. Few follow-ups: embedding dimensionality, candidate counts for initial retrieval, and whether you plan hybrid retrieval with BM25.
[01:03] Alex: We're using 1536-dim embeddings from an open model right now for parity with some open-source encoders; candidate set is usually 200, then we rerank top 20 with a cross-encoder.
[01:16] Jordan: OK, that matters. 1536 dims increases vector size and memory, impacts throughput; do you have an update frequency for your index?
[01:27] Nina: We update nightly full reindex, smaller incremental batches during the day — maybe 1k changes/hour at peak.
[01:35] Priya: Security is also a must: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and ideally a VPC/private deployment for PHI-ish metadata.
[01:46] Maya: Totally understood. We have Hosted for quick evals, Dedicated for reserved capacity and predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for data residency and KMS/HSM. Can I outline tradeoffs?
[01:58] Priya: Please.
[02:00] Maya: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value, lower overhead, but shared infra — good for non-PII. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable tail latency at your QPS, and isolation. Private gives the control you need for compliance — runs in your VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS.
[02:17] Alex: In terms of latency for rerank — we're seeing target p95 under 300ms for the cross-encoder stage. Is that achievable on Dedicated?
[02:26] Jordan: Short answer: yes, with the right model size and batching. For cross-encoder rerank we can run a trimmed quantized variant on GPU; typical p95s for a 2-3k token cross-encoder are sub-200ms on a Dedicated GPU if you're sending small batches, but it depends on model. The trick is to do coarse candidate retrieval (fast FAISS/Milvus) then run cross-encoder on top N, N~20-50.
[02:48] Nina: Gotchas around dimensionality — if we switch to 768 dims to save cost, we worry about retrieval quality drop. Any suggestion?
[02:56] Jordan: There's a tradeoff. Sometimes 768 is fine for recall if your content is dense; 1536 helps separability for long clinical notes. Another option is asymmetric encoding: use a smaller index vector for retrieval, then richer cross-encoder to recover quality. Also quantized vectors (8-bit) reduce footprint.
[03:16] Priya: What about hybrid search — BM25 + embeddings? We need keyword coverage for drug names and dates.
[03:23] Maya: Hybrid is common: initial BM25 filter to ensure exact term matches, then embedding re-rank for semantic relevance. Redwood supports routing so you can do BM25 as a prefilter (Elasticsearch or Postgres) then call embedding retrieval. We also have suggestions for combining scores and calibration.
[03:40] Alex: Throughput numbers — we expect bursts to 150 QPS and steady 60 QPS. Candidate retrieval is fast, but cross-encoder capacity is the limiter. What would you run for Dedicated?
[03:52] Jordan: For 150 QPS with cross-encoder rerank top-20, you'd typically need ~2 GPUs depending on model size and batching. If you push batching aggressively and use KV cache, you can get better token throughput but at some latency cost. We can prototype with your model to get exact numbers.
[04:12] Nina: Integration: how does Redwood connect to Milvus/Pinecone? Are there connectors or a push model?
[04:19] Maya: We provide an API for embedding generation and hosting; for retrieval you can keep your vector DB and call it directly, or use our integrated index if you prefer. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy connectors in your VPC to talk to Milvus/Weaviate and pull candidate sets, or you can push embeddings into Redwood's managed index.
[04:40] Priya: Data residency — we need logs to stay in our VPC and KMS for keys. Does Redwood support bringing your own KMS?
[04:48] Maya: Yes, for Private deployments you can use customer-managed KMS/HSM. Dedicated has options for private networking and audit logs. Hosted has encrypted-at-rest and SOC2 but not customer KMS. We'll share the security pack.
[05:00] Alex: For the reranker model, we prefer a distilled cross-encoder. Do you support model pinning and rollouts?
[05:07] Jordan: Yes, you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts; Redwood Optimize can also suggest quantization and batching settings per model/workload to hit latency/cost targets.
[05:19] Nina: Any sample numbers for cost? Even ballpark GPU counts per QPS?
[05:25] Maya: We'll include a rough cost sheet in the benchmark spreadsheet — depends on model, dims, and candidate size. For example, a single A10-like GPU for bi-encoder retrieval epochs might handle X, but cross-encoder rerank at top-20 is the expensive stage and scales with QPS. We'll model with your sample queries.
[05:44] Priya: About ops: we need index rebuild times and zero-downtime rollouts — how do you handle versioned indexes?
[05:51] Jordan: We support pinned versions and can do blue/green index swaps for low downtime; for large reindexes we recommend incremental updates and a fallback policy to older index if an issue is detected.
[06:05] Alex: A very practical question — embedding dimensionality in storage: do you support mixed dims across collections?
[06:12] Maya: Yes, collections can have different dims; you just need to ensure the retrieval pipeline knows which model/dim to call. It adds complexity but is common in multi-tenant datasets.
[06:24] Nina: Cross-talk: what about approximate nearest neighbor settings — HNSW params, efConstruction, efSearch — do you recommend defaults?
[06:32] Jordan: Defaults are fine to start: efSearch around 128 for good recall/latency. We'll share tuned recommendations based on your cardinality.
[06:43] Priya: Auditing — we need immutable logs for queries and rerank decisions for compliance.
[06:49] Maya: Audit logs are available in Dedicated/Private with retention options; Hosted has standard logs but for regulated workloads we push Dedicated/Private.
[06:59] Alex: One more: we do rerank A/B experiments and need rollout metrics tied to user queries — can Redwood emit traces for each request?
[07:07] Jordan: Yes, per-request tracing and token-level cost/latency breakdowns are supported in the Console; you can also export traces to your observability stack.
[07:18] Priya: Ok this is helpful. Can you walk through a proposed POC scope?
[07:24] Maya: Sure — typical POC: 1) Redwood runs a bench using your sample data (50k docs, 2k queries) to measure retrieval+rerank latency and quality; 2) We validate integration with your vector DB (Milvus) in a test VPC; 3) We evaluate Dedicated config to meet p95 targets; 4) Security review with your compliance team. That usually takes 2-3 weeks.
[07:48] Alex: For bench metrics we care about Recall@20, MRR, p50/p95 latency, and cost per 1k queries.
[07:57] Jordan: Good, we'll capture those. We'll also measure embedding generation time if you use our hosted embedder versus self-host.
[08:07] Nina: Small nit: our queries sometimes include regex-like filters and exact tokens — we need to ensure hybrid step preserves that.
[08:14] Maya: Recommend prefiltering with BM25 or Postgres to force exact matches, then do embedding retrieval on the filtered subset. We'll include an example flow in the doc.
[08:27] Priya: Any red flags?
[08:29] Jordan: Only that cross-encoder rerank at high QPS is the cost driver. If budget is tight, consider richer bi-encoder + asymmetric rerank or distillation to smaller cross-encoders. Also watch index cardinality and efSearch.
[08:43] Alex: Do you have customers in healthcare doing PHI work in Private?
[08:48] Maya: Yes, a couple — we can anonymize case studies in the security pack.
[08:54] Priya: Cool. Let's recap next steps.
[08:57] Maya: Recap: we share benchmark spreadsheet + security pack, customer shares sample dataset and query logs, schedule POC scoping. Also Jordan will draft architecture.
[09:07] Alex: Sounds good.
[09:09] Nina: Anything else?
[09:11] Maya: We'll target the doc send by Jan 4th and follow up with calendar invites. Thanks all.
[09:18] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:21] [call ends]
